mainTopic: Finishing the פרה אדומה cases, the rules and measures of pausing during שחיטה (שהייה), and a new משנה on flawed שחיטות that make an animal a נבלה or a טרפה.
overview: The amud finishes רבא's rules about a פרה אדומה slaughtered together with something else. An animal slaughtered with it by accident depends on the מחלוקת between רבי נתן and רבנן. A gourd cut on purpose ruins the פרה according to everyone, and a gourd cut by accident does not. Then a new משנה teaches that a pause (שהייה) in the middle of שחיטה makes it invalid. The תנא קמא measures the pause as 'כדי שחיטה' and רבי שמעון measures it as 'כדי ביקור'. The גמרא brings several opinions on how long 'כדי שחיטה' is, including רב, שמואל, רבי יוחנן, רבי חנניא and the scholars of ארץ ישראל. רבא rules that slow, nonstop cutting with a blunt knife is kosher. Questions about pauses that add up and a pause during the last part of the סימנין are raised and not resolved. The amud closes with a new משנה on flawed שחיטות (נבלה or טרפה), and the גמרא begins a contradiction that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Another animal was slaughtered by accident along with the red heifer
steps.stepSummary: רבא continues: if a second animal got slaughtered along with the פרה without intent, the outcome depends on the מחלוקת between רבי נתן and רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If another animal was slaughtered together with it: according to רבי נתן, the פרה is invalid and the animal is kosher. According to רבנן, the פרה is valid and the animal is not kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is continuing רבא's statement from before. It gives the result when a second animal was slaughtered by accident in the same cut as the פרה אדומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן holds that slaughter without intent still counts. So the second animal is kosher, and that extra slaughter counts as additional work that ruins the פרה. רבנן hold it does not count as שחיטה, so no extra work was done: the פרה stays valid and the animal is not kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, the פרה אדומה (red heifer) used to make purifying ashes
Was slaughtered (it just happened, without intending it)
Invalid, disqualified
Valid, kosher

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the results are opposite. Whatever makes the extra animal kosher (it counts as real שחיטה) is exactly what ruins the פרה, because now extra work was done with it.

phrases.english: If another animal was slaughtered along with it,
phrases.notes: The word נשחטה means it happened by itself, without his intending to slaughter the second animal.

phrases.english: according to רבי נתן – the heifer is invalid
and the animal is kosher,
according to the Rabbis – the heifer is valid
and the animal is not kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's list of cases from the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי נתן, the פרה is invalid and the other animal is kosher. According to רבנן, the פרה is valid and the other animal is not kosher.

steps.title: Why say something so obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: this result follows simply from the known מחלוקת, so why did רבא need to teach it?
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that רבא's ruling seems obvious. It is setting up the next step, which will explain why the ruling was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know רבי נתן and רבנן disagree about slaughter without intent, and we already know extra work ruins a פרה. Putting the two together seems automatic, so the גמרא asks what new point רבא is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (a challenge that a statement teaches nothing new)

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether step 1 teaches anything new.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The result follows directly from rules we already know, so it seems unnecessary to say it.

steps.title: The point is that even an ordinary animal ruins the heifer
steps.stepSummary: The ruling was needed for רבי נתן's view. Without it, one might think the פסוק 'ושחט אותה' only rules out slaughtering two פרות together, not a פרה with an ordinary animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case where another animal was slaughtered was needed according to רבי נתן. You might have thought: the תורה says 'and he shall slaughter it', meaning not it together with another. And what case would that be? When one slaughtered two פרות at the same time. But an ordinary חולין animal, you might say, does not ruin it. So רבא teaches us that it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' challenge. It explains the mistake רבא wanted to stop us from making.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'ושחט אותה' teaches: slaughter it alone, not it and another. One might have read 'another' as meaning only a second פרה. רבא teaches that even an ordinary חולין animal slaughtered with it ruins the פרה, according to רבי נתן.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed for him (to teach)
You might have thought (the mistaken first idea)
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
An ordinary, non-holy animal
So it teaches us (the new point)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule against slaughtering the פרה together with another is not limited to two פרות.

phrases.english: The case of another animal slaughtered, according to רבי נתן,
was needed for him to teach,
since it might enter your mind to say:
The Merciful One said: 'And he shall slaughter it,'
meaning not it together with its fellow,
and what is the case?

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁשָּׁחַט שְׁתֵּי פָּרוֹת בַּהֲדֵי הֲדָדֵי,
phrases.english: For example, where he slaughtered two heifers at the same time,
but with an ordinary animal, I might say it does not,
so he teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִשְׁחֲטָה בְּהֵמָה אַחֶרֶת לְרַבִּי נָתָן אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows the ruling blocks a reasonable mistake
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק 'ושחט אותה, not it and its fellow' only rules out slaughtering two פרות together.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even an ordinary חולין animal slaughtered with the פרה ruins it, according to רבי נתן.

steps.title: Cutting a gourd together with the heifer
steps.stepSummary: If he cut a gourd on purpose along with the פרה, everyone agrees it is invalid. If the gourd got cut by accident, everyone agrees it is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he cut a gourd along with it, everyone agrees it is invalid. If a gourd was cut along with it, everyone agrees it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds one more case: a gourd cut in the same motion as the slaughter. Here there is no מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is whether he did it on purpose (חתך) or whether it just happened (נחתכה). Cutting on purpose is extra work, which ruins the פרה. An accidental cut of a gourd is not work that ruins it, and a gourd is not 'another' in the sense of the פסוק, so even רבי נתן agrees it stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: A gourd
He cut (on purpose)
It got cut (by itself, without intent)
Everyone agrees

steps.whatToRemember: With the פרה, what matters is extra work. An animal slaughtered by accident depends on the מחלוקת. A gourd cut on purpose ruins it, and a gourd cut by accident does not.

phrases.english: If he cut a gourd along with it –
everyone agrees it is invalid,
if a gourd got cut along with it –
everyone agrees it is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further case to רבא's list, one where there is no מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A gourd cut on purpose ruins the פרה. A gourd cut by accident does not, according to everyone.

steps.title: New משנה: pausing in the middle of slaughtering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists interruptions during שחיטה. If the pause lasted as long as a slaughter, the slaughter is invalid. רבי שמעון measures the pause by the time of an examination.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If the knife fell and he picked it up, or his garments fell and he picked them up, or he sharpened the knife and got tired and his friend came and finished slaughtering: if he paused for the length of a slaughter, it is invalid. רבי שמעון says: if he paused for the length of an examination.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new subject: an interruption (שהייה) in the middle of slaughtering. It gives examples and sets how long a pause makes the animal invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The examples are all pauses where the cut was stopped and then picked up again. The תנא קמא sets the limit at the time it takes to do a שחיטה. רבי שמעון uses a different measure, the time of a ביקור (examination).

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the abbreviation מתני׳ marks where it starts)
He paused or interrupted (the source of the term שְׁהִיָּה)
He sharpened
He grew weary
The length of time a slaughter takes
An examination

steps.whyThisMatters: שהייה, pausing in the middle, is one of the basic things that make a שחיטה invalid, and the גמרא will now discuss how long it is.
steps.confusionAlert: Here כליו means his clothes, not his tools or vessels.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If the knife fell and he picked it up,
his garments fell and he picked them up,
he sharpened the knife and grew tired,
and his friend came and slaughtered,
if he paused for the length of a slaughter – it is invalid.
רבי שמעון says:
if he paused for the length of an examination.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה on a new topic, unrelated to the פרה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pause in the middle of slaughter that lasts as long as a שחיטה makes it invalid. רבי שמעון measures the pause by the time of a ביקור.

steps.title: What does 'the time of a slaughter' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking what the משנה means by כדי שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is meant by 'as long as a slaughter'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks a simple clarifying question about the משנה's measurement. It is setting up the answer that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that a pause lasting as long as a slaughter makes the שחיטה invalid. It did not say which slaughter it means. The גמרא wants to know exactly what amount of time is being measured.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
As long as it takes to slaughter; the length of pause that invalidates
What is; used to ask for the meaning of a term

phrases.english: Gemara:
What is 'as long as a slaughter'?
phrases.notes: This refers back to the משנה's rule about pausing in the middle of the cut.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts explaining the measurement given in the משנה in Step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact length of time meant by כדי שחיטה.

steps.title: The time it takes to slaughter another animal
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that the measure is the time it takes to slaughter a different animal from start to finish.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It means as long as it takes to slaughter another animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question. The pause is measured by how long a whole new slaughter would take.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might have thought the measure was just the time needed to finish the cut that was interrupted. רב says no: you picture slaughtering a fresh animal from the beginning. That is a fixed and longer measure.

keyTerms.meaning: The slaughter of a different animal
Pausing in the middle of the cut
An animal, such as a cow or a sheep

phrases.english: Rav said:
As long as the slaughter of another animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: כְּדֵי שְׁחִיטַת בְּהֵמָה אַחֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The measure is the time needed to slaughter another animal.

steps.title: Is a bird measured by a bird or by an animal?
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא and רב אסי ask רב whether each kind is measured by its own kind, or whether even a bird is measured by the time of slaughtering an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא and רב אסי said to רב: Is it the time of slaughtering an animal for an animal and a bird for a bird? Or perhaps even the time of slaughtering an animal for a bird?
steps.whatsHappening: Two students ask רב a follow-up question about his answer. They want to know which 'other animal' is the measure when the thing being slaughtered is a bird.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal's neck is thicker, so slaughtering it takes longer than slaughtering a bird. If a bird is measured by a bird, a short pause already invalidates it. If even a bird is measured by an animal, a bird's slaughter stays valid unless the pause is longer.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird
An animal is measured by an animal, and a bird by a bird
Or perhaps; brings the second side of a question
Even a bird is measured by the time of slaughtering an animal

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי לְרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana and Rav Asi said to Rav:
Is it as long as the slaughter of an animal for an animal,
and of a bird for a bird,
or perhaps even of an animal for a bird?
phrases.notes: So when slaughtering a bird, the pause would be measured by the longer time of slaughtering an animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי לְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for more detail about רב's answer in Step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the measure for a bird is the time of a bird's slaughter or the longer time of an animal's slaughter.

steps.title: רב never asked his teacher
steps.stepSummary: רב says he did not feel close enough to his beloved teacher to ask him this question, so he has no answer to pass on.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I was not close enough with my beloved one to ask him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers, but he does not settle the question. He explains that he only knows what he heard and never asked about this detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב is passing on a tradition he received, and that tradition did not cover the bird question. Because he never asked his teacher, the question stays open for now. The next step shows how the אמוראים later ruled on it.

keyTerms.meaning: Relaxed and at ease; close enough to speak freely
My beloved one
That I could ask him

phrases.english: He said to them:
I was not at ease with my beloved one,
phrases.notes: רב uses 'my beloved one' for his uncle and teacher, רבי חייא.

phrases.english: that I could ask him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the question in Step 8 without settling it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No ruling. רב did not have the information, because he never asked his teacher.

steps.title: The dispute: each kind by its own kind, or even a bird by an animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports a מחלוקת. רב holds an animal is measured by an animal and a bird by a bird. שמואל, and רבי יוחנן as reported by רבין, hold that even a bird is measured by an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב said, as long as the slaughter of an animal for an animal and a bird for a bird. שמואל said, even an animal for a bird. And likewise, when רבין came, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: even an animal for a bird.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a recorded מחלוקת on the exact question רב could not answer. רב rules one way, while שמואל and רבי יוחנן rule the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds each kind is measured by its own kind, so a bird is invalidated by a shorter pause. שמואל and רבי יוחנן use the longer animal measure even for a bird, which is more lenient for birds. Now two major אמוראים stand against רב on this point.

keyTerms.meaning: Even for a bird, measure by an animal's slaughter
A disagreement between sages
A set legal measure or amount

steps.whatToRemember: A pause invalidates שחיטה if it lasts as long as slaughtering another animal. רב: animal for animal, bird for bird. שמואל and רבי יוחנן: even a bird is measured by an animal.
steps.confusionAlert: Here רב takes a clear position. In Step 9 he only said he had not heard it from his teacher. This step reports how he ruled on his own.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav said:
As long as the slaughter of an animal for an animal,
and of a bird for a bird,
and Shmuel said: Even of an animal for a bird,
and likewise, when Ravin came
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even of an animal for a bird.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: אָמַר רַב: כְּדֵי שְׁחִיטַת בְּהֵמָה לִבְהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the question left open in Steps 8 and 9 was later ruled on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: each kind is measured by its own kind. שמואל and רבי יוחנן: even a bird is measured by the time of an animal's slaughter.
steps.whyThisMatters: This decides how long a pause makes a bird's שחיטה invalid. That is a practical question for every שוחט.

steps.title: רבי חנניא: Time to Bring Another Animal and Slaughter It
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניא gives another measure for the pause: the time it takes to bring a different animal and slaughter it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנניא said: the measure is the time it takes to bring another animal and slaughter it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a new opinion about the measure of the pause. רבי חנניא says it includes the time to bring a new animal, not just the time to slaughter one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב in Step 7 measured only the slaughtering itself. רבי חנניא makes the measure longer by adding the act of bringing the animal. That makes it easier for a שחיטה with a pause to stay kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: That he brings (another animal)
A different animal

phrases.english: Rabbi Chananya said:
The time it takes for him to bring another animal
and slaughter it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another opinion on the measure of כדי שחיטה, alongside רב's view and the views in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disqualifying pause is the time it takes to bring another animal and slaughter it.

steps.title: Challenge: Bringing From Anywhere Makes the Measure Unfixed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that if the measure includes bringing an animal from anywhere, the time would change from case to case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he mean bringing an animal even from anywhere in the world? Then you have made your rule depend on circumstances!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי חנניא. If the time includes bringing an animal from wherever one happens to be, there is no fixed measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A measure in הלכה should be the same for everyone. Bringing an animal could take a minute or a whole day, depending on where the nearest animal is. So רבי חנניא's rule as stated seems to have no fixed size.

keyTerms.meaning: From anywhere at all, from the outside world
You have made your words depend on circumstances, so there is no fixed measure

phrases.english: Does he bring it even from anywhere?
phrases.notes: In other words, does the time to fetch an animal from far away count too?

phrases.english: You have made your words subject to varying measures!
phrases.notes: The time would be different every time, depending on how far away the animal is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי חנניא's measure from Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנניא's measure that includes bringing another animal.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Bringing an animal takes a different amount of time in each case, so the rule would have no fixed amount.

steps.title: רב פפא: The Difference Is a Standing Animal That Must Be Thrown Down
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that רבי חנניא does not mean fetching from far away. He only adds the time to throw down an animal that is standing nearby.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: the difference between them is a standing animal that must be thrown to the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge. רבי חנניא's 'bringing' only means throwing down a standing animal, which is a fixed amount of time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנניא does not count the time of fetching from elsewhere, so his measure is fixed after all. The only difference from רב is whether we add the time to cast a standing animal onto the ground before slaughtering it. רבי חנניא adds that time, so his measure is a little longer.

keyTerms.meaning: Standing (the animal is upright)
To cast or throw down to the ground
There is a practical difference between them

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
A standing animal that must be thrown down
is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: עוֹמֶדֶת לְהַטִּיל אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12 by narrowing what רבי חנניא meant.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the meaning of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי חנניא counts the time to fetch an animal from anywhere, so his measure has no fixed size.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חנניא only adds the fixed time of throwing down a standing animal. That is the only difference between him and רב's measure.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי חנניא counts walking to get an animal. 'Bringing' here only means throwing down an animal that is already standing there.

steps.title: In the West: Lift, Lay Down and Slaughter, Small for Small and Large for Large
steps.stepSummary: The scholars of ארץ ישראל quote רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: the measure is the time to lift the animal, lay it down and slaughter it, matched to the animal's size.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said in the West in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא: the time it takes to lift it, lay it down and slaughter it; a small animal by a small one, and a large animal by a large one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more opinion about the measure of the pause. It comes from the scholars of ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view adds lifting and laying the animal down to the slaughtering time. It also says the measure depends on the size of the animal: a small animal like a sheep is measured by a small animal, and a large animal like a cow is measured by a large one.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל
That he lifts it up
And lays it down
A small animal, like a sheep or goat
A large animal, like a cow

steps.whatToRemember: There are several opinions on the length of the pause: רב (time to slaughter), רבי חנניא (also throwing down a standing animal), and the West (lift, lay down, slaughter, matched by size).

phrases.english: They said in the West
in the name of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina:
The time it takes to lift it, lay it down, and slaughter it,
a small animal by a small animal,
phrases.notes: The pause for a small animal is measured by how long these steps take for a small animal.

phrases.english: and a large animal by a large animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי בְּמַעְרְבָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another opinion on the measure, after the discussion of רבי חנניא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disqualifying pause is the time to lift, lay down and slaughter the animal, measured by an animal of the same size.

steps.title: רבא: Slaughtering With a Blunt Knife Is Valid Even If It Takes All Day
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that slow, continuous slaughtering with a poor knife is kosher, no matter how long it takes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: one who slaughters with a bad knife, even if it takes the entire day, the animal is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling. A long, slow שחיטה is fine, because the problem the earlier opinions discussed is a pause, not slowness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps measured how long a stop in the middle can be. Here the cutting never stops; it is just slow because the knife is not sharp. So the length of time alone does not make the שחיטה invalid.

keyTerms.meaning: A bad knife, one that is blunt or does not cut well
The entire day
Valid, kosher

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up slow cutting with stopping. The earlier measures are about a pause in the middle. רבא is talking about cutting that keeps going, only slowly.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the problem with a pause is the stop itself, not how much time the whole שחיטה takes.

phrases.english: Rava said:
One who slaughters with a bad knife,
phrases.notes: He means a dull knife that cuts slowly.

phrases.english: even if it takes the entire day,
it is kosher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from measuring a pause to a new case: slow but nonstop cutting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering with a blunt knife is valid even if it lasts the whole day.

steps.title: Do several short pauses add up?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether many small pauses during one שחיטה combine into one forbidden pause.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: if there were several short pauses, do they add up together?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks a new question. Each pause on its own is too short to make the animal not kosher. Do they count together?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 7-14 gave a measure for how long a pause can be. רבא now asks what happens if no single pause reaches that measure, but all the pauses together do. If they add up, the שחיטה is not kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked a question that he did not know the answer to
Pauses, stops in the middle of the שחיטה
Do they join together and count as one?

phrases.english: Rava asked:
Pauses, do they join together?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting the length of a forbidden pause, the גמרא asks whether short pauses can add up to it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether separate short pauses add up to a forbidden שהייה.

steps.title: Answer it from רבא's own ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רבא's slow-knife ruling already answers his question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him answer it from his own ruling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the question. רבא himself ruled that a long, slow שחיטה is kosher, so why is he asking?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 15, רבא allowed a slow שחיטה with a poor knife, even if it lasts all day. A long cut like that probably has small breaks in it. So it seems small breaks do not add up, and his question should already be answered.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him solve it
From his own words

phrases.english: And let him solve it from his own statement!
phrases.notes: This points back to step 15, where רבא allowed a slow שחיטה that goes on for a long time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the question in step 16 using רבא's ruling from step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's question about pauses adding up
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A daylong slow שחיטה surely has small breaks, and רבא called it kosher. So small breaks must not add up.

steps.title: That ruling had no pause at all
steps.stepSummary: The slow-knife case was one nonstop motion, so it tells us nothing about pauses.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he did not pause.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. In the slow-knife case the שוחט never stopped moving the knife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slow cutting is not the same as pausing. In step 15 the knife kept moving back and forth the whole time, so there were no pauses to add up. רבא's question about real pauses is still open.

keyTerms.meaning: There, in that other case
Where he did not pause

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'slow' with 'stopping'. A slow שחיטה that never stops is kosher however long it takes. The question is only about real stops.

phrases.english: There, it is where he did not pause.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: no pause at all versus several pauses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The slow-knife case had small pauses, so pauses do not add up.
steps.terutzMaskana: The slow-knife case had no pauses, so רבא's question remains open.

steps.title: A pause while cutting the last small part
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן asks about a pause after most of the סימנין were already cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן asked: if he paused during the minority of the סימנין, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question. Most of the סימנין are already cut, which is enough for שחיטה. Then the שוחט pauses before cutting the rest. Does that pause ruin the שחיטה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting most of the סימנין already makes the שחיטה kosher. So maybe a pause afterward does not matter. Or maybe the whole cutting still counts as one act, so a pause anywhere in it is a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The smaller part of the סימנים (windpipe and food pipe) that is left after most was cut
He paused

phrases.aramaic: בָּעֵי רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Natan asked:
If he paused during the minority of the simanim, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question about pauses, this time about when the pause happens.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a pause after most of the סימנין are cut makes the שחיטה not kosher.

steps.title: The question is left open
steps.stepSummary: The question is not answered: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: It stands unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds no answer, so the question stays open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תיקו means the גמרא found no proof either way. So we do not know whether a pause during the last small part of the סימנין ruins the שחיטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it stand. The question is left without an answer.

phrases.english: Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the question from step 19 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a pause during the last small part of the סימנין ruins the שחיטה is left as an open question.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's measure from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי שמעון in the משנה: a pause the length of an examination makes the שחיטה not kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: if he paused for the time of an examination.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes רבי שמעון's measure for a pause. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier measures (steps 6-14) explained the תנא קמא's 'כדי שחיטה'. Now the גמרא turns to רבי שמעון's different measure, 'כדי ביקור', which it will explain next.

keyTerms.meaning: The time it takes to examine (the knife)

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
If he paused [for the time of an examination].
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording, finishing רבי שמעון's words from the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the תנא קמא's measure to רבי שמעון's measure in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pause as long as an examination makes the שחיטה not kosher.

steps.title: What does 'כדי ביקור' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'the time of an examination' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'the time of an examination'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an exact meaning of רבי שמעון's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'An examination' is vague. Examination of what, and by whom? The גמרא needs a fixed amount of time.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it?

phrases.english: What is 'the time of an examination'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the term in step 21 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact length of time meant by 'כדי ביקור'.

steps.title: The time a חכם takes to examine
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says it means the time of a חכם's examination of the knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: the time of a חכם's examination.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers that the measure is how long it takes a חכם to check the knife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before שחיטה, the knife was brought to a חכם to check that it had no nicks. רבי יוחנן says the forbidden pause is the length of that check.

keyTerms.meaning: The examination done by a חכם

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The time of the examination of a Sage.
phrases.notes: This means checking the knife before the שחיטה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כְּדֵי בִּיקֻּרוֹ שֶׁל חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The time it takes to bring the knife to a חכם and have him check it.

steps.title: That time would change every time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the time to reach a חכם is different in each case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, you have made your words depend on changing measures!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's answer. A rule needs one fixed measure, and this one keeps changing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sometimes the חכם is nearby and sometimes he is far away. Then the length of the pause would change each time. This is the same kind of problem the גמרא raised in step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
You made your rule depend on measures that change from case to case

phrases.english: If so,
You have given your words over to changing measures!
phrases.notes: He means the time would depend on how far away the חכם happens to be.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's explanation in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's explanation of כדי ביקור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Travel time to a חכם changes, so the measure would not be fixed.

steps.title: A slaughterer who is a חכם
steps.stepSummary: The measure is the time a slaughterer who is himself a חכם takes to check his knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the time of an examination by a slaughterer who is a חכם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem. The measure is a שוחט who is a חכם himself, so nobody has to travel.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שוחט can check his own knife, there is no travel time. Only the checking itself counts, and that is about the same every time. Now the measure is fixed, just like רב פפא's fix in step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It brings in a corrected explanation.
A slaughterer who is also a חכם

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's measure for a pause, 'כדי ביקור', is the time a שוחט who is a חכם takes to check his own knife. Travel time is not counted, so the measure stays the same.

phrases.english: Rather,
The time of an examination by a slaughterer who is a Sage.
phrases.notes: He checks his own knife right there, so no time is spent going to someone else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 24 by changing who does the examination.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition: the examiner is the שוחט himself, so there is no travel time
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The time includes bringing the knife to a חכם, so it changes from case to case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the checking itself counts, done by a שוחט who is a חכם, so the time is fixed.

steps.title: Four ways a שחיטה goes wrong, and the argument about them
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists four flawed שחיטות. רבי ישבב says the animal is a נבלה. רבי עקיבא says it is a טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone cut the gullet properly but tore the windpipe, or tore the windpipe first and then cut the gullet, or cut one סימן and waited until the animal died, or hid the knife under the second סימן and cut it from below: רבי ישבב says it is a נבלה, and רבי עקיבא says it is a טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists four cases where the שחיטה was not done right and brings an argument about what status the animal has.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In every case, at least one סימן was not cut in a kosher way. The argument is only about which kind of forbidden animal it is. A נבלה is a carcass that also gives off טומאה. A טרפה is forbidden to eat but does not give off טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The gullet (food pipe), one of the two סימנים
The windpipe, the other סימן
Tore or chopped through it, not by the proper back-and-forth slaughtering cut
Hid the knife underneath the סימן while cutting (חֲלָדָה)
An animal that was not validly slaughtered; forbidden to eat, and it gives off טומאה
An animal forbidden to eat, but it does not give off טומאה like a נבלה

steps.confusionAlert: Both נבלה and טרפה are forbidden to eat. The argument here is not about whether you may eat the animal. It is about which category it falls into, and only a נבלה gives off טומאה.

phrases.english: MISHNA:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט אֶת הַוֶּושֶׁט, וּפָסַק אֶת הַגַּרְגֶּרֶת,
phrases.english: If one slaughtered the gullet properly and tore through the windpipe,
phrases.notes: "Tore" means he did not use the normal back-and-forth slaughtering cut on that סימן.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ פָסַק אֶת הַגַּרְגֶּרֶת וְאַחַר כָּךְ שָׁחַט אֶת הַוֶּושֶׁט,
phrases.english: or tore through the windpipe and afterward slaughtered the gullet,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שָׁחַט אֶחָד מֵהֶן וְהִמְתִּין לָהּ עַד שֶׁמֵּתָה,
phrases.english: or slaughtered one of them and waited until it died,
phrases.notes: "One of them" means one of the two סימנים, the gullet or the windpipe.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ שֶׁהֶחְלִיד אֶת הַסַּכִּין תַּחַת הַשֵּׁנִי וּפְסָקוֹ –
phrases.english: or hid the knife underneath the second one and cut it from below,
Rabbi Yeshevav says: it is a neveila (carcass);
Rabbi Akiva says: it is a tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ שָׁחַט אֶת הַוֶּושֶׁט, וּפָסַק אֶת הַגַּרְגֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the previous discussion of רבי שמעון's measure for a pause.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In these four flawed שחיטות, רבי ישבב rules the animal is a נבלה and רבי עקיבא rules it is a טרפה.

steps.title: The general rule: a bad שחיטה makes a נבלה, another cause makes a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישבב gives a rule in the name of רבי יהושע: a flawed שחיטה makes a נבלה, and a proper שחיטה with another problem makes a טרפה. רבי עקיבא agreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישבב stated a rule in the name of רבי יהושע: any animal that became unfit through its שחיטה is a נבלה. Any animal whose שחיטה was proper, but something else made it unfit, is a טרפה. And רבי עקיבא agreed with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a general rule that explains רבי ישבב's view. Then it says that רבי עקיבא agreed with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule asks one question: where did the problem come from? If the שחיטה itself was done wrong, it never counted as a שחיטה, so the animal is a נבלה. If the שחיטה was good but some other defect made the animal unfit, it is a טרפה. Since רבי עקיבא agrees, the four cases in the משנה end up as נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule that covers many cases
Properly, the way it should be done
And he agreed with him (he changed his mind)

steps.whatToRemember: A flaw in the שחיטה itself makes the animal a נבלה. A good שחיטה with some other defect makes it a טרפה. רבי עקיבא ends up agreeing.
steps.whyThisMatters: The words "רבי עקיבא agreed" are exactly what the גמרא will now question by bringing a contradicting source.

phrases.aramaic: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי יְשֵׁבָב מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yeshevav stated a principle in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:
any animal that was disqualified in its slaughter is a neveila;
any animal whose slaughter was done properly

phrases.aramaic: וְדָבָר אַחֵר גָּרַם לָהּ לִיפָּסֵל – טְרֵפָה,
phrases.english: and something else caused it to become unfit is a tereifa.
And Rabbi Akiva conceded to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלָל אָמַר רַבִּי יְשֵׁבָב מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רבי ישבב's ruling in step 26 and reports that רבי עקיבא accepted it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A flawed שחיטה makes the animal a נבלה. A proper שחיטה followed by another defect makes it a טרפה. רבי עקיבא agrees.

steps.title: The גמרא sets up a contradiction from the list of טרפות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and starts to raise a contradiction from another משנה that begins "These are the טרפות in an animal."
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "If he slaughtered the gullet," and so on, up to "and רבי עקיבא agreed with him." But there is a contradiction from another משנה: "These are the טרפות in an animal."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes our משנה and then starts bringing another משנה that seems to clash with it. This line is a setup; the actual clash will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The other משנה is a list of injuries that make an animal a טרפה. The גמרא is about to show that something in that list does not fit the ruling here, where רבי עקיבא agreed the animal is a נבלה. The details of the contradiction come on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: And they pointed out a contradiction: another source seems to say the opposite
"These are the טרפות," the opening words of a list of defects that make an animal forbidden
"Etc." The rest of the quoted line is skipped for short

phrases.english: GEMARA:
"If one slaughtered the gullet," etc.
"And Rabbi Akiva conceded to him."
And raise a contradiction: "These are tereifot in an animal:"
phrases.notes: This is the opening of the משנה at the start of the next פרק, which lists defects that make an animal a טרפה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a challenge against the משנה's ruling in steps 26 and 27, especially רבי עקיבא's agreement.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה's ruling, which רבי עקיבא accepted, that these flawed שחיטות make the animal a נבלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה lists defects that make an animal a טרפה, and something in that list will be shown to conflict with calling these cases נבלה. The contradiction is completed on the next amud.
